text: STATE-DRIFT RETRO (round-61, requested by Andrey via Orchestrator — root cause and prevention, no blame). HOW IT ESCAPED, four gaps: (1) TESTING — plan mutations are tested as field writes, not as CONTRACTS: nothing asserted 'in_progress implies pane', 'in_review implies report', so status theater passed every suite; the mirror bug was fixed once (task_354c755f) WITHOUT a standing concurrent-write suite, so it regressed invisibly. (2) PROCESS — statuses are self-reported claims with no verification layer; gating throughput relied on one orchestrator's serial attention; the In-QA queue existed (task_49f03e58, done) and went UNUSED — second occurrence of shipped-but-unadopted (plan skills was the first): machinery that isn't wired into prompts/process does not exist. (3) PROMPT/REPORTING — report templates carry branch/sha as PROSE; nothing binds pane/peer at claim time (11/13 pane-less, peer empty on ALL tasks incl. mesh lanes). (4) SCHEMA/API — no write-time invariants: the store accepted in_progress without pane, and #209's pane update silently didn't take (root-cause owned by task_7140a28c). META ROOT CAUSE: the plan store was built as a recording system for agent claims, not a supervised state machine — every drift class follows from that single design stance. PREVENTION, three layers now filed + one process rule: write-time invariants (task_7140a28c, P1), continuous observation (this watchdog, P1), atomic dispatch composition (task_310d7e6b, P2), gate wiring + adoption enforcement (task_<gate-wiring>, P2 — incl. counting In-QA adoption in the reflection loop). Feeds the plan retrospective as a first-class input alongside the polling incident and the planner self-retro.

USER FRAMING PINNED VERBATIM (round-62, clarification — this overrides any drift toward auto-transitions): agents moving the core statuses (todo/in_progress/in_review/blocked/done) is CORRECT and stays untouched — that is not the problem being solved. The watchdog answers ONE question: 'is the assignee actually working?' — an ORTHOGONAL observed-liveness dimension rendered NEXT TO the agent-set status, never replacing it. Staleness thresholds apply to the OBSERVED signal (executor idle/silent too long), not to status age itself: a task may sit in_progress for days legitimately while its executor observably works. Any implementation that auto-moves core statuses violates this task's intent and bounces.

SHARED-CHECKOUT RETRO (round-67, Andrey's question via Orchestrator: HOW was there no gate preventing workers editing the main checkout?). Honest answer, three compounding causes: (1) ISOLATION WAS PROSE — worktree-per-lane lived in AGENTS.md and task role_guidance; not one enforcement point existed in spawn, report, or daemon paths. Rules without affordances/enforcement lose to friction (same finding as the polling incident — this is now the plan's central lesson). (2) ALARM FATIGUE BY DESIGN — the daemon's own sidecar churn (.codeterm/plans/**) keeps every checkout permanently dirty, so the ONE existing guard (dirty-worktree report refusal) cried wolf constantly; workers learned to acknowledge/bypass, and real unrelated-dirty violations rode through the same door. The system trained the behavior it then suffered from. (3) ADOPTION DEBT — QA queue existed unused (3rd occurrence). PREVENTION SHIPPED AS TASKS: spawn guard task_46d7cc4c (Worker into canonical checkout refused without recorded exception — BEFORE RELEASE), sidecar churn task_4fc2ae89 (Phase 1 dirt-check exclusions BEFORE RELEASE + Phase 2 decision gate for Andrey on plans-in-git), report refusal hardening + code-only + build detection (task_5a6d58c5), worktree ownership visibility folded into plan lanes (task_d1450940 — added: flag two live lanes sharing one cwd as a collision). RELEASE VERDICT: 46d7cc4c + 4fc2ae89-Phase1 + 5a6d58c5 are release-gating (they make the remaining endgame gates trustworthy); dispatch/lanes commands stay post-release.

RETRO — why non-QA panes still built AFTER the agreement (round-70, Orchestrator self-ask, honest answer): (1) THE AGREEMENT WAS CHAT — the interim rule lived in messages to you, not in any worker's spawn prompt: every worker spawned before (and even after) the rule was born with the OLD worker_suffix that literally demands BUILD/TYPECHECK/TESTS results in reports — the form kept asking, so workers kept building; a rule stated to the orchestrator does not propagate to already-alive workers or to templates. (2) NOTHING WATCHED — build-detection (5a6d58c5) is filed, not landed; between agreement and enforcement there is a window where only memory holds, and memory loses under load — the third occurrence of the same meta-lesson. (3) YOUR QA RUNNER COEXISTS with capable workers: registering b813bb47 as the runner changed nothing about what OTHER panes could do. ENFORCEMENT THAT CLOSES IT (all filed): QA-pane registry singleton + registry-keyed build detection (5a6d58c5, sharpened this round), rewritten report template (same task), spawn guard (46d7cc4c). FUTURE-PLANNER GUARANTEE: these land in product code + wiring-tested templates — a future agent cannot repeat this by forgetting, only by explicitly recorded exception. Interim until 5a6d58c5 lands: when dispatching ANY worker, prepend the code-only line in the task prompt itself (not chat), since the template still asks for builds.
